summary: Rusk County, Wisconsin lookout listed as gone by the Forest Fire Lookout Association; no build or removal dates found.

facts.status_note: Listed as gone by the Forest Fire Lookout Association.

evidence.supports: Scott in Rusk County at 45.53522 -90.98876, tower gone

evidence.quote: Wisconsin once had a vast fire tower lookout network

evidence.supports: lookout took a bearing with a compass table and called in direction and distance
evidence.quote: If a smoke was sighted, the lookout used a compass table situated at the center of the cab

evidence.supports: other towers reported the same smoke so the dispatch center could locate it
evidence.quote: Other towers in the network would identify and report the same smoke
At the height of their use, 119 towers dotted the landscape.

evidence.supports: many standing towers built in the 1930s by CCC crews
evidence.quote: Many of the towers we see still standing today were built during the 1930s by the young men of the Civilian Conservation Corps.

evidence.supports: 72 towers still in use decommissioned in 2015
evidence.quote: In 2015, the 72 aging towers still in use were decommissioned.

evidence.supports: Wisconsin decommissioned its lookout network in 2015
evidence.quote: until 2015 when Wisconsin decommissioned its lookout network

evidence.supports: Wikipedia dates the state's decision to close its last 72 towers to 2016

sources.title: Connecting the dots: the fire towers of Wisconsin

notes_for_editor: Thin record. The Forest Fire Lookout Association list gives only location, county and gone status. No build date, design, staffing, access or removal date was found in two web searches and the cached pages. The statewide paragraph is context, not a claim about when Scott came down; the 2015 (WJFW, NHLR) and 2016 (Wikipedia) decommissioning dates disagree. Not on the Central US Lookouts Wisconsin list. Worth checking a Wisconsin DNR or Rusk County source, and recent aerial imagery, before the site is described as having any remains.
